Clustering NBA players utilizing K-Means, Gaussian Mixture Models, Principal Component Analysis and Graphical Networks


Next we will cluster types of defenders
```{r}
df_def <- read.csv("data/defensive_tracking.csv", stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
df_adv<-read.csv("data/ad.csv", stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
colnames(df_def)
colnames(df_adv)
```


```{r}
clean_duplicates <- function(df) {
  df %>%
    group_by(Player) %>%
    # If a player has multiple rows, keep the one where Team is 'TOT' (Total)
    # If they only have one row, keep it.
    filter(n() == 1 | Team == "2TM") %>%
    ungroup()
}

df_adv <- clean_duplicates(df_adv)
df_adv <- df_adv %>%
  rename(PLAYER_NAME = Player)


# 4. Merge the Tables Together
# We join by Player, Pos, and Age to ensure perfectly matched rows
merged_data <- df_def %>%
  inner_join(df_adv, by = c("PLAYER_NAME")) 
```




```{r}
# 1. Load Libraries
library(dplyr)
library(tidyr)
library(factoextra)

library(dplyr)
library(factoextra) # Great package for visualizing clusters

# 1. Select the most descriptive columns for clustering
clustering_data <- df_def %>%
  select(
    # VOLUME (Defensive Workload & Location)
    D_FGA_OVERALL,   # Total shots contested
    FGA_LT_06_6FT,   # Rim protection volume
    FG3A_3P,         # Perimeter defense volume
    
    # EFFICIENCY (Impact relative to expected)
    #PCT_PLUSMINUS_OVERALL, # Overall defensive impact
    #PLUSMINUS_6FT,         # Rim deterrence 
    #PLUSMINUS_3P           # Perimeter deterrence
  ) %>%
  # Fill any lingering NAs with 0 just to be safe
  mutate(across(everything(), ~tidyr::replace_na(.x, 0)))

# 2. Scale the data (Z-Score Normalization)
# This centers everything around 0 so the algorithm treats all stats equally
scaled_clustering_data <- scale(clustering_data)

# Let's verify the scaling worked
head(scaled_clustering_data)

# 7. Find Optimal K (Plot the elbow)
fviz_nbclust(scaled_clustering_data, kmeans, method = "wss")+ 
  labs(title = "Elbow Method for Defender Archetypes")

```
Not using a library and doing the for loop explicitly

```{r}
# 7. Find Optimal K (Manual SSE Loop)
set.seed(222) 
MAX_K <- 10 # Capped at 10 to prevent micro-clusters
sse <- c() 


for (k in 1:MAX_K) {
  algo_k <- kmeans(scaled_clustering_data, centers=k, nstart=22, iter.max=20) 
  sse <- c(sse, algo_k$tot.withinss) 
}

# Plot the elbow
plot(1:MAX_K, sse, type="b", pch=19, col="blue",
     xlab="Number of clusters K", 
     ylab="Total within-clusters sum of squares (SSE)")
```

This now takes the 1st derivative

```{r}
tibble(k = 1:MAX_K, SSE_difference = sse-lead(sse)) %>%
  dplyr::filter(k<MAX_K) %>%
  ggplot(aes(x=k, y=SSE_difference)) + 
  geom_point(color="#F84C1E") + geom_line(color="#232D4B") + # set color of point and lines
  labs(x = "K", y = "SSE Rolling Difference", title = "A Clearer Picture") + # set axis/plot titles
  scale_x_continuous(breaks=seq(1, MAX_K, 1)) + # define x-axis
  theme(panel.grid.minor.x = element_blank(), panel.grid.minor.y = element_blank()) # manually alter theme
```

Now we will take the 2nd derivative

```{r}
tibble(k = 1:MAX_K, SSE_difference = sse-2*lead(sse)+lead(sse, 2)) %>%
  dplyr::filter(k<MAX_K-1) %>%
  ggplot(aes(x=k, y=SSE_difference)) + 
  geom_point(color="#F84C1E") + geom_line(color="#232D4B") + 
  labs(x = "K", y = "SSE Rolling 2-Unit Difference", title = "An Even Clearer Picture") + 
  scale_x_continuous(breaks=seq(1, MAX_K, 1)) + 
  theme(panel.grid.minor.x = element_blank(), panel.grid.minor.y = element_blank())
```
I will go with k=5 clusters

```{r}
# 1. Run Final K-Means with K = 5
set.seed(222) # Keeping your seed for reproducibility
final_defender_kmeans <- kmeans(scaled_clustering_data, centers = 5, nstart = 25)

# 2. Attach the cluster labels back to your original unscaled data
df_def$Defender_Cluster <- as.factor(final_defender_kmeans$cluster)

# 3. Calculate the average stats for each cluster to see what they represent
cluster_profiles <- df_def %>%
  group_by(Defender_Cluster) %>%
  summarise(
    Count = n(),
    # Volume: Where are they defending?
    Avg_Total_Contests = round(mean(D_FGA_OVERALL), 1),
    Avg_Rim_Contests = round(mean(FGA_LT_06_6FT), 1),
    Avg_3P_Contests = round(mean(FG3A_3P), 1),
    
    # Efficiency: How much are they lowering the opponent's FG%? (Negative is better!)
    Avg_Overall_Impact = round(mean(PCT_PLUSMINUS_OVERALL), 3),
    Avg_Rim_Impact = round(mean(PLUSMINUS_6FT), 3),
    Avg_3P_Impact = round(mean(PLUSMINUS_3P), 3)
  )

# Print the profiles to the console
print(cluster_profiles)

# 4. Export the mapping for Python / PyTorch
# We only need the Player name and their Cluster ID to merge into your shot log
defender_export <- df_def %>%
  select(PLAYER_NAME, Defender_Cluster)

write.csv(defender_export, "defender_archetypes_15_16.csv", row.names = FALSE)
```


```{r}
# 1. Crear el vector de nombres de columnas (asegúrate de que coincida con tus datos)
features_names <- c("USG.", "FGA_per100", "AST_per100", "Dist", "X3PAr", 
                    "pct_FGA_0_3", "pct_FGA_3_10", "pct_FGA_10_16", "pct_FGA_3P", 
                    "pct_3PA_Corner", "pct_FGA_Dunks", "pct_Ast_2P", "pct_Ast_3P")

# 2. Asignar nombres a las columnas de los centros y añadir la columna Cluster
km_centers <- as.data.frame(final_shooter_kmeans$centers)
colnames(km_centers) <- features_names # Asigna los nombres al DF
km_centers$Cluster <- c('Cluster 1', 'Cluster 2', 'Cluster 3', 'Cluster 4', 'Cluster 5')

# 3. Pivotar a formato largo para que ggplot reconozca 'feature' y 'z_val'
km_centers_long <- km_centers %>% 
  pivot_longer(cols = -Cluster, names_to = "feature", values_to = "z_val")

# 4. Tu código de ggplot (usando km_centers_long)
km_centers_long %>% 
  ggplot(aes(x = feature, y = z_val, color = Cluster)) + 
  geom_point() + 
  scale_color_brewer(palette = "Paired") + 
  gghighlight(use_direct_label = FALSE) + 
  facet_wrap(~ Cluster, ncol = 3) + 
  labs(x = "Predictor", y = "Cluster Center (Z-score)", 
       title = "Visualizing K-Means Cluster Makeups") + 
  theme_minimal() + # Sugerido para limpieza visual
  theme(legend.position = "none", 
        strip.text = element_text(face = 'bold'),
        axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 90, size = 8, vjust = 0.5, hjust = 1), 
        panel.grid.minor = element_blank())
```


```{r}
pca <- prcomp(scaled_clustering_data) # perform Principle Component Analysis 
pca_summary <- summary(pca) # summary of PCA model

# plot % of variance between players explained by each subsequent PC 
tibble(imp = pca_summary$importance[2,], n = 1:length(imp)) %>% # get importance scores for PCA summary
  ggplot(aes(x=n, y=imp)) + 
  labs(x = 'Principle Component #', y = '% of Variance Explained by Component',
       title = 'Less Information is Gained by Each Subsequent PC') +
  geom_point(color="#F84C1E") + geom_line(color="#232D4B") + 
   scale_x_continuous(breaks=seq(1, 20, 1)) + # set x-axis
  scale_y_continuous(labels=scales::percent) + # change y-axis from proportion to percentage
  theme(panel.grid.minor.x = element_blank(), panel.grid.minor.y = element_blank())
```


```{r}
pc2 <- as.data.frame(pca$x[,1:3]) # extract first 3 PCs
pc2$Cluster <- as.factor(final_defender_kmeans$cluster) # add player clusters 
cluster1_var <- round(pca_summary$importance[2,1], 4) * 100 # get variance explained by cluster 1
cluster2_var <- round(pca_summary$importance[2,2], 4) * 100 # get variance explained by cluster 2

# how different are the clusters when scaled down to two dimensions? 
pc2 %>% 
  ggplot(aes(x=PC1, y=PC2, color=Cluster, shape=Cluster)) + 
  geom_point(alpha=0.3) + 
  scale_color_futurama() + # fun color scale
  geom_rug() + # great way to visualize points on a single axis
  stat_ellipse(level=(2/3)) + # set ellipse value to one standard deviation
  scale_shape_manual(values=seq(0,15)) + 
  labs(x = paste0('PC1 (Accounts for ', cluster1_var, '% of Variance)'), # define cluster 1 % of variance
       y = paste0('PC2 (Accounts for ', cluster2_var, '% of Variance)'), # define cluster 2 % of variance
       title = 'Visualizing K-Means Cluster Differences in 2D') 
```


Gaussian mixture model


```{r}
# run GMM on the scaled data from above
set.seed(222)
mixture_model <-  Mclust(pca$x[,1:4])
mix_model_summary <- summary(mixture_model) # obtain model summary
mix_model_summary
```



```{r}
library(dplyr)
library(tidyr)
library(ggplot2)

# 1. Get the MAP class labels from your PCA-trained GMM
# 1. Get the MAP class labels from your PCA-trained GMM
gmm_labels <- mixture_model$classification

# 2. Bind those labels to your ORIGINAL scaled data (so we have basketball stats, not PCs)
gmm_profiles <- as.data.frame(scaled_clustering_data) %>%
  mutate(Cluster = paste("Cluster", gmm_labels))

# 3. Calculate the true centers (means) for each feature by Cluster
mbc_centers <- gmm_profiles %>%
  group_by(Cluster) %>%
  summarise(across(everything(), mean))

# 4. Pivot for plotting (exactly as you wrote it!)
mbc_centers_long <- mbc_centers %>%
  pivot_longer(!Cluster, names_to = 'feature', values_to = 'z_val')

# 5. Plot the Z-Score Profiles [This creates a beautiful line chart of your archetypes]
ggplot(mbc_centers_long, aes(x = feature, y = z_val, color = Cluster, group = Cluster)) +
  geom_point(size = 3) +
  geom_line(linewidth = 1) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 0, linetype = "dashed", color = "black") + # 0 is the NBA average
  theme_minimal() +
  facet_wrap(~ Cluster, ncol = 5) +
  coord_flip() +
  labs(title = "GMM Cluster Profiles (Z-Scores)",
       x = "Offensive Feature",
       y = "Standard Deviations from NBA Average") +
  theme(axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 45, hjust = 1))
```

```{r}
# changing the .class assignment in this chunk of code allows you to explore the players with the highest probability of belonging to that cluster
library(broom)
library(dplyr)

pca_embeddings <- as.data.frame(pca$x[, 1:4])


mix_model_preds <- as.data.frame(predict(mixture_model, pca_embeddings))
mix_model_augment <- augment(mixture_model, df_def)
# Extract the Top 5 purest representatives for ALL 5 clusters instantly
top_5_per_cluster <- mix_model_augment %>%
  dplyr::select(Player, .class, .uncertainty) %>%
  group_by(.class) %>%
  arrange(.uncertainty) %>%      # Ascending: Lowest uncertainty = purest fit
  slice_head(n = 5) %>%          # Grab the top 5 from each group
  ungroup()                      # Always ungroup when done!

# Print all 25 rows to the console
print(top_5_per_cluster, n = 25)
```

```{r}
library(mclust)
library(dplyr)
library(broom)

# 1. Run the GMM on the first 4 Principal Components
# CRITICAL: We add G = 5 so it outputs exactly 5 archetypes to match your offense
set.seed(222)
mixture_model <- Mclust(pca$x[,1:4], G = 5)

# 2. Extract the soft labels (Probability Matrix)
# This is an N x 5 matrix of probabilities
gmm_probs <- as.data.frame(mixture_model$z)

# 3. Rename the columns so they are clean for Python
colnames(gmm_probs) <- c("Def_Prob_Cluster_1", "Def_Prob_Cluster_2", 
                         "Def_Prob_Cluster_3", "Def_Prob_Cluster_4", "Def_Prob_Cluster_5")

# 4. Bind the actual player names back to the probabilities
# Note: Ensure 'df_def' has a column named 'PLAYER_NAME' (or change this to match your ID column)
gmm_export <- cbind(Player = df_def$PLAYER_NAME, gmm_probs)

# 5. Let's look at the top pure archetype for each cluster to see what the model found!
mix_model_augment <- augment(mixture_model, df_def)

top_5_per_cluster <- mix_model_augment %>%
  dplyr::select(PLAYER_NAME, .class, .uncertainty) %>%
  group_by(.class) %>%
  arrange(.uncertainty) %>%      # Lowest uncertainty = purest fit
  slice_head(n = 5) %>%          # Grab top 5 pure defenders per cluster
  ungroup()

print("Top Purest Defenders by Archetype:")
print(top_5_per_cluster, n = 25)

# 6. Export the final clean CSV for PyTorch/XGBoost
write.csv(gmm_export, "gmm_soft_labels_def_15_16.csv", row.names = FALSE)
```


```{r}
# Load necessary libraries
library(dplyr)
library(tidyr)
library(mclust)

# 1. Feature Engineering & Transformation
# Ensure your df_def dataframe has the advanced stats merged in before running this
df_def_clean <- merged_data %>%
  # Fill any NAs with 0 to prevent Mclust from breaking
  mutate(across(everything(), ~tidyr::replace_na(.x, 0))) %>%
  mutate(
    # Fix the extreme right-skew of defensive volume metrics
    Rim_Vol_Trans = sqrt(FGA_LT_06_6FT),
    Perimeter_Vol_Trans = sqrt(FG3A_3P),
    Total_Vol_Trans = sqrt(D_FGA_OVERALL),
    
    # Compress the extreme right-skew of elite shot blockers
    BLK_PCT_Trans = sqrt(BLK.) 
  )

# 2. Select the final 9 metrics (Volume + Impact + Discipline)
clustering_data <- df_def_clean %>%
  select(
    # --- VOLUME ---
    Rim_Vol_Trans, 
    Perimeter_Vol_Trans, 
    Total_Vol_Trans,
    
    # --- EFFICACY / IMPACT ---
    PCT_PLUSMINUS_OVERALL, 
    PLUSMINUS_6FT, 
    PLUSMINUS_3P,
    
    # --- PLAYMAKING & DISCIPLINE ---
    BLK_PCT_Trans, 
    STL., 
    #PF_per100  # Personal fouls per 100 possessions (or Foul Rate)
  )

# 3. Scale the Data (Z-Score Normalization)
scaled_clustering_data <- scale(clustering_data)

# 4. Run the Gaussian Mixture Model
set.seed(222)
# Mclust will automatically find the optimal number of clusters using BIC
mixture_model_def <- Mclust(scaled_clustering_data) 

# Attach the hard labels back to your dataframe for EDA and profiling
df_def_clean$Def_GMM_Cluster <- as.factor(mixture_model_def$classification)

# 5. Calculate Average Stats per Cluster (Using raw stats for readability)
cluster_profiles_def <- df_def_clean %>%
  group_by(Def_GMM_Cluster) %>%
  summarise(
    Count = n(),
    
    # Volume Profile
    Avg_Total_Contests = round(mean(D_FGA_OVERALL), 1),
    Avg_Rim_Contests = round(mean(FGA_LT_06_6FT), 1),
    Avg_3P_Contests = round(mean(FG3A_3P), 1),
    
    # Impact Profile (Negative = good defense)
    Avg_Overall_Impact = round(mean(PCT_PLUSMINUS_OVERALL), 3),
    Avg_Rim_Impact = round(mean(PLUSMINUS_6FT), 3),
    Avg_3P_Impact = round(mean(PLUSMINUS_3P), 3),
    
    # Playmaking & Discipline Profile
    Avg_BLK_PCT = round(mean(BLK.), 3),
    Avg_STL_PCT = round(mean(STL.), 3),
    #Avg_PF_per100 = round(mean(PF_per100), 1)
  )

# Print profiles to the console so you can define the archetypes for your thesis
print("Defensive Archetype Profiles:")
print(cluster_profiles_def)

# Save human-readable profiles for your appendix
#rite.csv(cluster_profiles_def, "gmm_defensive_profiles_15_16.csv", row.names = FALSE)


# 6. Export the Soft Labels for XGBoost / PyTorch
```

```{r}
library(dplyr)
library(tidyr)
library(ggplot2)

# 1. Get the MAP class labels from your trained GMM
gmm_labels <- mixture_model$classification

# 2. Bind those labels to your ORIGINAL scaled data and assign Archetype names
gmm_profiles <- as.data.frame(scaled_data) %>%
  mutate(Cluster = factor(gmm_labels, 
                          levels = c(1, 2, 3, 4), 
                          labels = c("Elite Rim Protector", 
                                     "Point of Attack Disruptors", 
                                     "Vulnerable Defenders", 
                                     "Versatile Forwards")))

# 3. Calculate the true centers (means) for each feature by Cluster
mbc_centers <- gmm_profiles %>%
  group_by(Cluster) %>%
  summarise(across(everything(), mean))

# 4. Pivot for plotting
mbc_centers_long <- mbc_centers %>%
  pivot_longer(!Cluster, names_to = 'feature', values_to = 'z_val')

# 5. Plot the Z-Score Profiles
ggplot(mbc_centers_long, aes(x = feature, y = z_val, color = Cluster, group = Cluster)) +
  geom_point(size = 3) +
  geom_line(linewidth = 1) +
  facet_wrap(~ Cluster, ncol = 4) + # Updated to 4 columns
  coord_flip() +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 0, linetype = "dashed", color = "black") + # 0 is the NBA average
  theme_minimal() +
  labs(title = "Defensive Archetype Profiles (Z-Scores)",
       x = "Defensive Feature",
       y = "Standard Deviations from NBA Average") +
  theme(axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 45, hjust = 1),
        legend.position = "none") # Hides redundant legend
```
